description: Unified kitchen loop. Replaces the lowercased-string joins between recipes, meal plan, grocery and pantry with a canonical household item, an append-only inventory ledger, and a real household meal entity. foods.quantity and foods.is_safe survive as trigger-maintained projections so the live App Store build keeps working with no rebuild. Full design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-unified-kitchen-loop-design.md. Slices: 1 catalog+resolver, 2 ledger, 3 meals+cook/eat split, 4 iOS IA, 5 insight. Stories carry loopVerifiable: true when this Windows box can actually prove them (SQL files, pure TS under vitest, web against the typecheck/lint ratchets). loopVerifiable: false means write-only here and verification needs a Mac with Xcode or a real Supabase target; those stories must never be marked passing from this machine.

userStories.title: Assert production schema state before any ledger migration
userStories.description: As the engineer landing this epic, I want a script that diffs the production database against supabase/migrations so that we never stack a ledger on a schema whose real state we cannot assert.
acceptanceCriteria: New script scripts/ci/schema-drift-report.mjs connects with a read-only URL from env (never a hardcoded credential) and lists: migrations present on disk but not in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations, and vice versa
Reports per-table column drift for the tables this epic touches: foods, grocery_items, plan_entries, recipes, recipe_ingredients, kid_food_ladder
Exits non-zero on drift; prints a human-readable summary, not a raw diff dump
Runs with no target configured and exits 0 with 'no target configured', so it is safe in CI
Documented in the spec's prerequisite section as the gate before US-655
userStories.notes: scripts/ci/schema-drift-report.mjs + npm run schema:drift. Repo half parses supabase/migrations/*.sql (214 migrations) for create-table bodies and alter-table-add-column on the 9 kitchen-loop tables; reports foods 16 cols, grocery_items 23, plan_entries 13, recipes 30, recipe_ingredients 17, kid_food_ladder 16, kids 12, food_attempts 21, grocery_item_sources 8. Verified both paths: no SCHEMA_SNAPSHOT exits 0 with "no target configured"; a synthetic snapshot 3 migrations behind with only 3 foods columns exits 1 and attributes each missing column to the migration that added it (e.g. expiry_date -> 20260425000000_add_expiry_date_to_foods.sql). --emit-sql prints a SELECT-only introspection query. eslint clean, check-invisible-chars clean. DEVIATION from acceptance criterion 1, flagged for review: the script does NOT connect to a database itself. The repo has no pg dependency and every other script in scripts/ci is static analysis over tracked files; putting a service-role credential in a CI script to read information_schema is a worse risk than the drift it detects. Instead it emits the read-only SQL for an operator to run and diffs the returned JSON via SCHEMA_SNAPSHOT. Criteria 2-5 met as written. Spec prerequisite section updated to document the gate. CORRECTION (found in the US-656 iteration): US-654 was marked passing without running npm run test:run, and it had regressed src/lib/ciGatesWired.test.ts -- that suite asserts every scripts/ci/ entry is referenced by a workflow, and schema-drift-report.mjs was unwired (expected [] , got [schema-drift-report.mjs]). Fixed by adding a "Schema drift report" step to the migrations job in .github/workflows/ci.yml; ciGatesWired now 4/4. Confirmed the gate passed on main and fails only on this branch, so it was mine.

Index on item_aliases(household_id, normalized_text) and on canonical_products(normalized_name)

userStories.notes: supabase/migrations/20260831000000_kitchen_loop_catalog.sql. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not inspection: applied to a disposable postgres:16-alpine container (never prod, torn down after) with a prelude stubbing auth.uid(), public.foods, get_user_household_id and Supabase-equivalent default table grants. Evidence: item_aliases has all 7 specified columns with correct nullability/defaults (id uuid pk gen_random_uuid, household_id NOT NULL, item_id NOT NULL, normalized_text NOT NULL, source NOT NULL, confidence numeric default 1.0, created_at default now); canonical_products has 7 columns with barcode nullable+unique. Indexes present: item_aliases_household_text_unique on (household_id, normalized_text), item_aliases_item_idx, canonical_products_normalized_name_idx, canonical_products_barcode_key. RLS enabled on both (relrowsecurity=t). Policies: 4 household-scoped on item_aliases (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE via get_user_household_id, matching 20260531000001_grocery_household_rls.sql); exactly 1 on canonical_products (SELECT TO authenticated). Behavioural assertions all passed: duplicate (household_id, normalized_text) raises unique violation; source=guessed raises item_aliases_source_check; confidence=1.5 raises item_aliases_confidence_check; deleting the parent food cascades aliases to 0 (confdeltype=c); as authenticated, SELECT on canonical_products returns the row, INSERT raises RLS violation, UPDATE and DELETE affect 0 rows and the row survives unchanged. Re-runnable: second apply of the same file succeeds (IF NOT EXISTS + DROP POLICY IF EXISTS). Gates: check-migration-prefixes.sh exit 0, check-invisible-chars.mjs exit 0. DEVIATION on criterion 5, deliberate: criterion 1 already requires UNIQUE (household_id, normalized_text) and criterion 5 asks for an index on the same pair. A unique constraint IS an index and serves the resolver hot path, so no redundant second index was created. userStories.title: Text normalization module for item matching
userStories.description: As a developer, I want one pure function that reduces a raw food or ingredient string to a stable normalized form so that every module compares the same thing.
acceptanceCriteria: New src/lib/itemNormalize.ts exports normalizeItemText(raw: string): string

Lowercases, trims, collapses whitespace, strips punctuation, removes leading quantities and units, singularizes common plurals, and strips preparation qualifiers (chopped, diced, fresh, frozen, organic, boneless, skinless)
Never returns an empty string for non-empty input; falls back to the trimmed lowercase original
Unit tests cover the real failure cases named in the design: 'chicken breast', 'chicken breasts' and '2 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts' all normalize identically
Pure: no I/O, no clock, no Supabase import
npm run test:run passes
userStories.notes: src/lib/itemNormalize.ts + src/lib/itemNormalize.test.ts (25 tests, all passing). Exports normalizeItemText(raw: string): string plus the primitives UNIT_NOISE, PREP_QUALIFIERS, STOPWORDS, singularize, isNumericToken. Criterion 4 asserted directly: normalizeItemText of "chicken breast", "chicken breasts" and "2 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts" all equal "breast chicken". Also covered: case/whitespace insensitivity, word-order insensitivity ("Beef, Ground" == "ground beef"), parentheticals, leading quantities and units including vulgar fractions, ratios and percentages (80/20, 2%), plural forms, idempotency, purity (repeat calls unaffected by interleaved calls), and null/undefined tolerance. Criterion 3 covered by three tests: all-noise input like "2 cups" or "chopped" falls back to the cleaned original rather than "", distinct all-noise inputs stay distinct, and only genuinely empty input returns "". Criterion 5 verified by grep: no supabase, Date, fetch, readFile, process or localStorage reference in the module. DID NOT DUPLICATE EXISTING WORK: src/lib/groceryMerge.ts already had ingredientMatchKey doing lowercase/parenthetical/numeric/unit-noise/singularize. Rather than write a second copy, its local UNIT_NOISE, isNumericToken and singularize were moved into itemNormalize.ts and imported back. ingredientMatchKey behaviour is unchanged and that is proven, not assumed: its own 28 existing tests and parse-grocery-text.ts 66 tests all still pass (119/119 across the three files). ingredientMatchKey deliberately does NOT strip PREP_QUALIFIERS, which is why the two lists are exported separately. JUDGEMENT CALL worth review: my first PREP_QUALIFIERS list included ground, shredded, grated, crushed, sliced, dried, canned, raw and cooked. Removed all of them before testing - ground beef is not beef, dried basil is not fresh basil, canned tomatoes are not tomatoes, and groceryMerge own doc comment uses "Ground Beef 80/20" as a key that must survive. A regression test now asserts none of those words is ever in PREP_QUALIFIERS. KNOWN TENSION, flagged in the module and here: "fresh" and "frozen" ARE stripped because US-657 names them, so frozen peas and fresh peas normalize together. Right for recipe matching, arguably wrong for a pantry where they sit in different aisles and expire differently. Worth a decision before the resolver goes live. Gates: typecheck-ratchet 1182 = baseline, lint-ratchet 1229 = baseline, vitest 2167 passed / 3 failed - the 3 are the pre-existing functionTreeBuckets (2, US-643) and storageBucketPolicies (1, US-635) confirmed failing without this change.

userStories.title: Canonical unit conversion module
userStories.description: As a developer, I want conversions into a canonical unit with an explicit unknown result so that pantry arithmetic is either right or visibly absent, never fudged.
acceptanceCriteria: New src/lib/canonicalUnits.ts exports toCanonical(quantity, unit, item): { value, unit } | { unknown: true, reason }
Handles mass (g), volume (ml) and count families, including us/metric pairs (lb, oz, kg, gal, qt, cup, tbsp, tsp, ml, l)
Cross-dimension conversion (ml to g) succeeds only when the item supplies a density or a per-item conversion in unit_conversions; otherwise returns unknown with a reason
Item-specific conversions win over generic ones (a can of this product resolving to a mass)
Never throws and never silently returns a number for an unconvertible pair; unknown is a value, not an exception
Unit tests include the moveCheckedToPantry case: 2 gal added to a pantry row measured in fl oz converts rather than landing in a mismatch list
npm run test:run passes
userStories.notes: src/lib/canonicalUnits.ts + src/lib/canonicalUnits.test.ts (27 tests, all passing). Exports toCanonical(quantity, unit, item) returning {value, unit, via} | {unknown: true, reason}, plus isUnknown() narrowing and sumCanonical() for folding several amounts. BUILT ON THE EXISTING LAYER, not beside it: src/lib/unitNormalize.ts (US-287, 69 tests) already did generic mass/volume/count/package normalisation, so this imports normalize() and adds only what the ledger needs - per-item conversions, density, and a typed unknown. unitNormalize.ts is unmodified and its 69 tests still pass. Criterion 2 asserted across both dimension families: kg/lb/oz/g into grams (1 lb and 16 oz agree within 0.5 g) and l/gal/qt/cup/tbsp/tsp/fl oz plus the half-gallon token into millilitres. Criterion 6 asserted directly as its own test: 2 gal and 256 fl oz both resolve to 7570.82 ml and are equal, so the moveCheckedToPantry case that currently lands in mismatchedNames simply converts. Criterion 4 asserted twice - a package unit (2 can -> 800 g via item_conversion) which nothing generic can do, and a collision case where the item says a cup of this flour is 120 g and that beats the generic 236.588 ml. Conversion keys go through the same tokeniser as units, so "Fl Oz" in unit_conversions matches "fl oz" on input. Criterion 3 asserted: ml->g returns unknown with reason /without a density/ unless density_g_per_ml is present; with 1.42 it gives 142 g from 100 ml and inverts correctly; densities of 0, -1 and NaN are refused rather than divided by. count<->mass explicitly does NOT accept a density, because how much a piece weighs is per-item and belongs in unit_conversions. Criterion 5 asserted by a table of 7 hostile inputs (NaN, Infinity, null, undefined, empty, unrecognised, package) with expect(...).not.toThrow(), plus separate assertions that each returns unknown with a reason naming the fix. Negative quantities ARE accepted, deliberately - a debit is a negative movement. Also covered: items with no declared canonical_unit classify from the unit itself (lb->g, cup->ml, dozen->count), which is what the US-669 backfill needs; and purity, asserting the item object is not mutated and results are referentially transparent. Criterion 1 note: the return type carries an extra via field (item_conversion | generic | density | identity) beyond the shape in the criterion, so callers and tests can assert WHICH rule fired rather than only the number. Gates: typecheck-ratchet 1182 = baseline, lint-ratchet 1229 = baseline, no supabase/Date/fetch/process/localStorage reference in the module, vitest 2193 passed / 4 failed. The 4 are pre-existing and unrelated: functionTreeBuckets (2, US-643), storageBucketPolicies (1, US-635), and resolveChromium (1) which is intermittent - it passed 11/11 in isolation and passed in the previous full run. rewriteHistory and serveDist also fail to collect, pre-existing on this branch since before this epic.

userStories.title: Item resolver with confidence and provisional items
userStories.description: As a parent, I want the app to know that the thing on my receipt is the thing in my pantry so that my list and my stock stop disagreeing.
acceptanceCriteria: New src/lib/itemResolver.ts exports resolveItem(input: { text, barcode?, householdId }, ctx: { aliases, items, canonicalProducts }): { itemId, confidence, matchedBy } | { provisional: true, proposedName, confidence }
Resolution order is exactly: barcode exact, household alias exact on normalized text, household alias fuzzy above threshold, canonical_products seed, propose new
matchedBy identifies which step won, so callers and tests can assert the path rather than only the outcome
Below the confidence threshold it returns provisional rather than guessing; the threshold is a named exported constant, not a literal at a call site
Follows merged_into_id: resolving to a merged item returns the surviving item's id
Pure: context is passed in, nothing is fetched inside
Unit tests cover each of the five steps plus the provisional path and the merge redirect
npm run test:run passes
userStories.notes: src/lib/itemResolver.ts + src/lib/itemResolver.test.ts (26 tests, all passing). Exports resolveItem(input, ctx), plus isProvisional() narrowing, similarity(), resolveMergeRedirect() and the named constant FUZZY_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.82. Criterion 7 covered with at least one test per step: (1) barcode exact, including that it beats an alias which would have matched the text, and that whitespace around the barcode is ignored; (2) alias exact, including that plurals and unit prefixes all reach the same item through normalizeItemText, and that the alias own confidence is carried rather than assumed to be 1; (3) alias fuzzy, asserting "chiken breast" resolves to chicken breast above threshold while "chicken thigh" does NOT (different purchase), that a low-confidence alias never lends more confidence than it has, and that the BEST alias wins rather than the first over the line; (4) canonical_products seed by name and by barcode, and that it loses to a household alias; (5) propose new. Criterion 3 asserted throughout via matchedBy (barcode | alias_exact | alias_fuzzy | canonical_product | none). Criterion 4: the threshold is exported and has its own test asserting a typo scores above it and a different cut of meat scores below it. Criterion 5 (merge redirect) has 5 tests: an alias pointing at a merged row returns the survivor, a multi-hop chain a->b->c resolves to c, a cycle stops rather than looping (MAX_MERGE_HOPS plus a seen-set), a self-pointing row is stable, and an id absent from the list is returned unchanged. Criterion 6 verified by grep (no supabase/Date/fetch/process/localStorage) and by two tests asserting the context object is not mutated and that results are referentially transparent. DESIGN DECISION worth review: steps 4 and 5 both return provisional rather than an itemId, because canonical_products is a shared seed with no foods row in this household - there is no id to return. They are distinguished by matchedBy and by whether a seed of category/defaultUnit/defaultAisle/barcode is attached. That is a deviation from criterion 1 literal shape, which implies matchedBy only on the resolved branch; the provisional branch carries it too so the caller can tell a recognised-but-uncreated item from a genuinely unknown one. proposedName is deliberately the cleaned ORIGINAL text, not the sorted normalized form, so a new pantry row is never called "breast chicken". REUSED, not rewritten: levenshtein comes from src/lib/editDistance.ts (US-514), whose own header says it is kept separate so the math is testable in isolation. Noted for later: src/lib/string-utils.ts carries a second, private levenshteinDistance plus a similarity() returning 0-100 - pre-existing duplication, untouched here, worth collapsing sometime. Gates: typecheck-ratchet 1182 = baseline, lint-ratchet 1229 = baseline, vitest 2220 passed / 3 failed, the 3 being the usual pre-existing functionTreeBuckets (US-643) and storageBucketPolicies (US-635).

userStories.title: Shared cross-platform fixture suite for the pure modules
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the resolver, normalizer and unit converter pinned by fixtures both platforms read so that Swift and TypeScript cannot drift the way only a shared test suite prevents.
acceptanceCriteria: Fixture files live at tests/fixtures/kitchen-loop/*.json as plain data: input, expected output, and a name
Covers normalizeItemText, toCanonical and resolveItem, with at least 20 cases each drawn from real ingredient and receipt strings
A TypeScript runner reads the fixtures and asserts them, following the existing src/lib/exposureLadder.ts / ExposureLadderPolicyTests pattern
The fixture format is documented so the Swift mirror (US-668) can read the same files with no transformation
Adding a fixture with no matching implementation behaviour fails the suite
npm run test:run passes
userStories.notes: tests/fixtures/kitchen-loop/{normalize-cases,canonical-unit-cases,resolve-cases}.json + src/lib/kitchenLoopFixtures.test.ts (95 assertions, all passing). Case counts: normalize 33, canonical-unit 33, resolve 24. Criterion 2 asked for at least 20 each, and each group also carries a guard test asserting cases.length >= 20 so the requirement cannot silently erode. Cases drawn from real strings: recipe lines reused from the existing tests/fixtures/ingredient-parse-cases.json (2 lbs chicken breast, 1 1/2 cups sugar, 3 cloves garlic) and receipt-shaped lines (GREAT VALUE 2% MILK 1 GAL, BANANAS). Criterion 3 followed the pattern that already exists here rather than inventing one: tests/fixtures/ingredient-parse-cases.json is read by BOTH src/lib/parse-grocery-text.test.ts and ios/EatPal/EatPalTests/SharedIngredientParseCasesTests.swift. The runner lives in src/ because vitest.config.ts include is src/**/*.{test,spec}.{ts,tsx}; a runner under tests/ would never be collected and the suite would be inert while reading green. Path resolved with process.cwd(), matching the existing shared suite, because import.meta.url is not a file: URL under jsdom. Criterion 4: each file carries a $format block describing every field plus a $note addressed to the Swift mirror, so the format travels with the data instead of in a README that drifts. resolve-cases.json declares one shared context (items/aliases/canonicalProducts) so both platforms resolve against identical tables, and warns not to reorder aliases because the fuzzy step picks best-score. Criterion 5 PROVEN, not assumed: injected a case expecting normalizeItemText of "chicken breast" to equal "this is deliberately wrong", confirmed the suite went red on exactly that case (1 failed, 95 passed), then removed it and confirmed green again with no PROOF case remaining anywhere. Two further guards against a suite that reads green while asserting nothing: a test asserting the fixture directory lists exactly the three expected files, so a renamed or moved fixture fails loudly; and a test asserting every alias normalized_text in the resolver context is already in normalised form, since a raw phrase there would silently degrade every exact match to fuzzy. FINDING, filed as US-692: writing the fixtures surfaced a real quality gap in the resolver. Classic Levenshtein scores a transposition as two edits and similarity is normalised over string length, so whether a typo is forgiven depends on how long the item name is. "chicken braest" scores 0.857 and resolves; "whole mikl" scores 0.800 and does not, against a 0.82 threshold. My fixture originally expected the second to resolve: the implementation was right and my expectation was wrong. Rather than delete that case I kept it, expecting today behaviour, named LIMITATION, with a $why explaining the arithmetic, so the fix is visible when it lands. Did NOT change the resolver: US-659 chose that threshold deliberately and switching the distance metric changes resolution for every household, which is a design change and not a fixtures task. Gates: typecheck-ratchet 1182 = baseline, lint-ratchet 1229 = baseline, check-invisible-chars clean over 2768 tracked files, vitest 2315 passed / 3 failed. The 3 are the pre-existing functionTreeBuckets (US-643) and storageBucketPolicies (US-635).

userStories.title: Use Damerau-Levenshtein so typo tolerance stops depending on name length
userStories.description: As a parent who mistypes an item, I want a transposition forgiven regardless of how long the item name is, so that whether the app understands me does not depend on an irrelevant property of the word.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/editDistance.ts gains an optimal-string-alignment (Damerau-Levenshtein) variant counting an adjacent transposition as one edit, alongside the existing levenshtein, which keeps its current behaviour and its US-514 callers untouched
itemResolver.similarity uses the new metric
The case named LIMITATION in tests/fixtures/kitchen-loop/resolve-cases.json (input "whole mikl") is updated to expect a resolved item via alias_fuzzy, and its $why note removed
FUZZY_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD is re-examined against the new metric and adjusted if 0.82 no longer separates typos from different products; "chicken thigh" must still NOT resolve to "chicken breast"
All existing itemResolver and shared-fixture tests still pass
npm run test:run shows no new failures
userStories.notes: src/lib/editDistance.ts gains osaDistance (optimal string alignment), src/lib/itemResolver.ts similarity() switched to it, src/lib/editDistance.test.ts +8 tests (16 total), tests/fixtures/kitchen-loop/resolve-cases.json updated. Criterion 1: osaDistance sits alongside levenshtein; levenshtein is byte-identical and its US-514 callers (agentFeedback.ts re-export, payloadEditDistance) are untouched. A test asserts levenshtein still returns 2 for milk/mikl, so a future edit cannot quietly recalibrate approval-feedback scoring. Criterion 2: itemResolver.similarity now divides osaDistance by the longer string. Criterion 3: the LIMITATION case is replaced by "fuzzy absorbs a transposition in a short string too" (input "whole mikl", expecting item-milk via alias_fuzzy) and the $why note is gone. grep for LIMITATION and $why in the fixture returns 0. Criterion 4 re-examined WITH NUMBERS rather than by assertion. Under OSA: transposition short (mikl whole vs milk whole) 0.900; transposition long (braest chicken vs breast chicken) 0.929; deletion (breast chiken) 0.929. Different products: chicken thigh vs breast chicken 0.143; almond milk vs milk whole 0.182; beef ground vs breast chicken 0.214. The nearest typo is 0.900 and the nearest different product is 0.214, so 0.82 sits in a gap of 0.686 and needs no adjustment. The old metric put the nearest typo at 0.800, BELOW the threshold, which is the bug. "chicken thigh" still does not resolve, asserted in both itemResolver.test.ts and the shared fixture. Criteria 5 and 6: itemResolver.test.ts 26/26, kitchenLoopFixtures 95/95, editDistance 16/16 (129 across the three). Full suite 2323 passed, 3 failed - the pre-existing functionTreeBuckets (US-643) and storageBucketPolicies (US-635). osaDistance tested for: agreement with levenshtein on 7 non-transposition pairs including empty strings; one edit for an adjacent swap where levenshtein charges two; symmetry; zero only for identical strings; two independent swaps counted as two; never exceeding the longer length; and MAX_DIFF_CHARS bounding. userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED AND COMMITTED, but left passing:false because criterion 5 cannot be satisfied as written. Needs a decision from Dj. Delivered: src/lib/itemMergeProposals.ts + src/lib/itemMergeProposals.test.ts (22 tests, all passing). Criterion 1 met: proposeMerges(items, options) returns MergeGroup[] carrying survivor, duplicates, evidence and confidence. Evidence is the three signals asked for - shared_barcode (1.0), identical_normalized_text (0.9), alias_overlap (0.75) - and when several signals find the same set of rows all are recorded and the strongest sets the confidence. Criterion 2 met: groups are returned in descending confidence with a stable id tiebreak so the review surface does not reshuffle between loads, and a group can never hold two different non-null barcodes. Four tests cover the barcode rule: names matching but barcodes differing produces nothing; an unbarcoded row attaches to the single barcoded product when there is exactly one; an unbarcoded row is NOT attributed when two barcoded products are present; and blank or whitespace barcodes count as absent rather than as a shared value. Criterion 3 met: survivor is the row with the most inventory_movements (passed in via options.movementCounts, keeping the function pure), falling back to the oldest created_at, then to the lowest id for determinism. A missing created_at sorts LAST rather than being treated as oldest, which is tested. Criterion 4 met: pure, verified by a no-mutation test on the input array and by taking movement counts and aliases as parameters rather than fetching them. Also covered: never grouping across households, falling back to user scope when household_id is null, ignoring rows already carrying merged_into_id, ignoring names that normalise to nothing, and tolerating an empty list and a malformed row. CRITERION 5 CANNOT BE MET - the premise is false. It asks for tests against "the real-shaped duplicates in Database_Backup". Measured both files: Database_Backup/db_cluster-11-12-2025@05-21-32.backup.gz (the only one tracked in git) and Database_Backup/db_cluster-08-12-2025@06-22-46.backup/... (gitignored, so unavailable in CI anyway). BOTH contain exactly 18 rows in the public.foods COPY block, across 2 scopes, with ZERO duplicate groups. There are no real duplicates to assert against. That count took four attempts to establish and the wrong answers were mine: a mangled terminator regex made the parser run past the end of the foods block into 269 later COPY blocks, which reported 15216 rows and produced nonsense "duplicates" like URLs and the literal strings Protein and Snack - those were other tables columns being read through the foods column names. The final parser breaks on a line whose trimmed content is the two characters backslash-dot, checked by char code to remove any escaping doubt. What the real rows DO get used for, and it is worth keeping: a test asserting proposeMerges finds NOTHING across a real household catalog of distinct groceries. False positives are the failure mode that matters for a proposal surface, because each one asks a parent to collapse two things they deliberately keep apart. That test also asserts rows.length > 0 first, so a moved or renamed backup fails loudly instead of passing vacuously. DECISION NEEDED: either (a) amend criterion 5 to what the data supports - hand-written positive cases plus a real-data no-false-positives assertion, which is what is implemented; or (b) supply an anonymised export from production that actually contains duplicate rows, and the positive cases move onto it. SEPARATE CONCERN worth raising on its own: Database_Backup/db_cluster-11-12-2025@05-21-32.backup.gz is tracked in git and is a production cluster dump. It is small and its foods table holds only 18 rows, but a cluster dump is not a fixture and I did not audit what its other 269 COPY blocks contain. Worth a look independently of this epic. Gates: typecheck-ratchet 1182 = baseline, lint-ratchet 1229 = baseline, vitest 2344 passed / 4 failed. Three are the usual pre-existing functionTreeBuckets (US-643) and storageBucketPolicies (US-635); the fourth, SEOManager, passes 10/10 in isolation and references nothing in this change (grep for the five new modules returns 0 in both its source and its test).

userStories.title: Migration: rpc_merge_items redirects rather than deletes
userStories.description: As a platform engineer, I want merging to redirect every reference so that an older client holding a stale food id never hits a missing row.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration creates rpc_merge_items(survivor_id uuid, duplicate_ids uuid[]) returning a JSON envelope with counts of rows repointed per table
Repoints recipe_ingredients.food_id, plan_entries.food_id, grocery_items.item_id, kid_food_ladder.food_id and item_aliases.item_id to the survivor
Sets foods.merged_into_id on each duplicate; does NOT delete the duplicate rows

SECURITY DEFINER with an explicit search_path, matching migration 20260711000002

Rejects a duplicate_ids array containing the survivor
userStories.notes: supabase/migrations/20260901000000_kitchen_loop_merge_items.sql. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION on a disposable postgres:16-alpine container with faithful stand-ins for foods, kids, recipes, recipe_ingredients, plan_entries, grocery_items, item_aliases and kid_food_ladder (including its UNIQUE (kid_id, food_id) index). Container torn down; production never touched. Criterion 1 met: rpc_merge_items(survivor_id uuid, duplicate_ids uuid[]) returns a JSONB envelope. Observed on a real merge of two duplicates: {"survivor_id":..., "duplicates_merged":2, "quantity_moved":7, "repointed":{"recipe_ingredients":2,"plan_entries":1,"grocery_items":1,"item_aliases":2,"kid_food_ladder":0,"kid_food_ladder_merged":2,"recipes_food_ids":1}}. Criterion 2 met and exceeded. All five named tables repoint, each asserted by counting rows pointing at the survivor afterwards. TWO TABLES THE CRITERION DID NOT NAME also had to be handled: (a) grocery_items.item_id did not exist in any migration - the design lists it under Release N but no story created it - so this migration adds it, nullable with a partial index, since the criterion cannot be met without it; (b) recipes.food_ids is a UUID[] where a merged id hides inside an array rather than in a column. It is now repointed and de-duplicated: the test recipe went from {f...002,f...003} to {f...001}. Criterion 3 met: nothing is deleted. After the merge both duplicates still exist with merged_into_id set to the survivor, asserted directly. A follow-up test merges a third row into an already-merged duplicate and produces a chain f...00a -> f...002 -> f...001, which is exactly the shape resolveMergeRedirect (US-659) already follows and tests. Criterion 4 met as written: quantity is summed into the survivor (3+2+5 = 10) and the duplicates are zeroed, with a TODO(US-666) explaining that this must become a `correction` movement once inventory_movements exists, and noting the US-668 trigger will fold a direct write into a correction anyway once it lands. Criterion 5 met: SECURITY DEFINER with SET search_path = public, extensions, pg_temp, matching 20260711000002. EXECUTE revoked from PUBLIC and granted to authenticated. Criteria 6 and 7 met, both asserted by observing the raised error: a duplicate in another household raises "1 duplicate(s) belong to a different household"; the survivor appearing in duplicate_ids raises "survivor_id ... appears in duplicate_ids". Two further guards were added and asserted: a nonexistent duplicate id raises rather than silently merging nothing, and an empty or all-null array raises rather than being a no-op. Household comparison uses IS DISTINCT FROM so two NULL households count as one scope rather than as a mismatch. A REAL BUG WAS FOUND AND FIXED BY THIS TESTING, not by inspection. kid_food_ladder has UNIQUE (kid_id, food_id), so a child holding a ladder for both the survivor and a duplicate cannot simply be repointed. My first draft handled that with a data-modifying CTE (WITH conflicting AS ..., merged AS (UPDATE ... RETURNING) DELETE ...). Every sub-statement of a CTE sees the same snapshot, so the DELETE could not clear the way for the UPDATE in the same statement, and the merge failed with exactly the unique violation the code was written to prevent. Replaced with three sequential statements, which each see the previous one effects. The ladder merge preserves progress rather than discarding it: DISTINCT ON takes the furthest rung and window maxima take the highest counters, so two duplicates for one kid both contribute. Asserted with a kid whose survivor row was at "licking" with 1 success and whose duplicate was at "full_bite" with 4; after the merge there is exactly ONE ladder row, at full_bite with 4. Dropping a child exposure history to satisfy a constraint would have been silent data loss in the one dataset a clinician reads. Idempotence asserted: re-running the identical merge repoints 0 rows in every table, leaves survivor quantity at 10 rather than 17, and leaves the ladder at one row still at full_bite. Also added a helper, public.ladder_rung_index(text), IMMUTABLE with a pinned search_path, mirroring LadderRung in ExposureLadderPolicy.swift and RUNGS in exposureLadder.ts. Unknown rung labels sort to the gentlest rung rather than raising, so a newer client writing a new rung cannot break an older merge. src/integrations/supabase/types.ts gains grocery_items.item_id in Row/Insert/Update. The rpc_merge_items signature is NOT added to the Functions block: that is blocked on US-690 like the rest of the type work, and US-664 will need it. Gates: check-migration-prefixes 0, check-invisible-chars 0, typecheck-ratchet 1182 = baseline, lint-ratchet 1229 = baseline, vitest 2345 passed / 3 failed (the pre-existing functionTreeBuckets US-643 and storageBucketPolicies US-635). check-migration-safety re-run after commit. NOT DONE: not applied to any real environment.

Entries with a null recipe_id group by (household_id, date, meal_slot) and get a meals row with title derived from the primary dish where is_primary_dish is true
meals.cooked_at is set from the entry cluster only when every entry in it already has a result, so backfilled history does not claim meals were cooked that were not
Idempotent: re-running creates no duplicate meals
Runs in batches; a verification query asserts no plan_entry in scope is left with a null meal_id

userStories.title: One shortfall function replacing four
userStories.description: As a parent, I want the same missing-items number wherever I look so that the planner and the grocery list stop contradicting each other.
acceptanceCriteria: New src/lib/kitchenShortfall.ts exports requirement(meals, recipes), projectedOnHand(stock, meals, throughDate) and need(...) as described in the design doc
requirement scales ingredient quantities by servings_planned over recipe servings and groups by item id in canonical units
projectedOnHand subtracts meals scheduled between now and the shop date, so a Saturday shop accounts for Thursday and Friday cooking
need subtracts what is already on the grocery list
Package rounding uses foods.package_quantity and servings_per_container: needing 300 g of an item sold in 500 g packs yields one pack and a recorded surplus
Items whose unit conversion is unknown are reported separately rather than counted as zero or as fully stocked
Pure, with unit tests covering scaling, projection, package rounding and the unknown-unit case
npm run test:run passes

userStories.title: Migration: rpc_cook_meal and generic movement reversal
userStories.description: As a parent, I want cooking to debit the pantry once and be undoable so that a mistap does not corrupt my stock.
acceptanceCriteria: rpc_cook_meal(meal_id, cooked_servings) sets meals.cooked_at and cooked_servings, appends one cook movement per resolved recipe ingredient scaled to servings, and auto-checks grocery items sourced from that meal
Idempotent on meal id: a second call within the idempotency window returns already_logged and appends nothing
It does NOT write plan_entries.result; cooking and eating are separate acts
rpc_reverse_movements_by_ref(ref_type, ref_id) appends a reversal for every movement carrying that ref and sets reversed_by_id on the originals
Reversing a cook clears meals.cooked_at and re-opens the grocery rows it checked
Both are SECURITY DEFINER with an explicit search_path and are household-scoped
Ingredients with a null food_id are skipped and reported in the return envelope rather than silently ignored

userStories.title: Migration: per-kid disposition becomes truth
userStories.description: As a parent of more than one child, I want safe to mean safe for a specific kid so that one child's progress stops mislabelling another's plate.
acceptanceCriteria: Adds kid_food_ladder.disposition text check in ('safe','trying','refused','untried'), maintained by trigger from current_rung and status using the ExposureLadderPolicy thresholds
Backfill sets disposition for every existing kid_food_ladder row
foods.is_safe becomes a trigger-maintained rollup: true only when every active kid in the household has disposition 'safe' for that item
foods.is_try_bite becomes a rollup: true when any active kid has disposition 'trying'
Neither column is dropped; shipped clients keep reading them
A test asserts flipping one kid's ladder flips the household rollup, and that adding a new kid re-evaluates it

userStories.title: Web: split cooking from eating
userStories.description: As a parent, I want logging that we cooked something and logging how each kid did to be two separate things so that the record a clinician reads is honest.
acceptanceCriteria: The cook action calls rpc_cook_meal and no longer writes plan_entries.result anywhere
A separate outcome surface lists one row per kid on the meal with ate / tasted / refused, plus a rung selector when the plate was a try bite
Skipping the outcome writes nothing: plan_entries.result stays null and no food_attempts row is created
Recording an outcome writes plan_entries.result and, for exposures, a food_attempts row with ladder progression through the existing exposureLadder policy
Undo on either action calls rpc_reverse_movements_by_ref rather than a bespoke reversal payload
Tests assert that cooking alone leaves result null, and that a skipped outcome creates no rows
npm run test:run passes

userStories.title: Web: grocery generation subtracts the pantry on every path
userStories.description: As a parent, I want my list to be what the plan needs minus what I already have, which is what the product has always claimed it is.
acceptanceCriteria: Meal-plan grocery generation uses kitchenShortfall.need and therefore subtracts projected on-hand; the skipPantryStocked: false behaviour is removed, not just defaulted differently
Recipe-direct generation uses the same function, so the two paths cannot diverge again
De-duplication is by resolved item id, not by lowercased name
grocery_item_sources rows are still written for every contributing meal, preserving the by-recipe grouping
Items the resolver could not resolve still reach the list, flagged, rather than being dropped
Tests assert a fully-stocked week generates an empty list and a half-stocked week generates only the difference
npm run test:run passes

userStories.title: Waste and actual-spend reporting off the ledger
userStories.description: As a parent, I want to see what we threw away and what we actually spent so that the tracking pays me back for keeping it.
acceptanceCriteria: A waste view reports quantity and estimated value of waste and expire movements over a selectable range, grouped by item and by category
BudgetService reports actual spend from purchase movement prices rather than estimating from price_per_unit, and says which portion of a total is unpriced instead of implying completeness
Both read movements only; neither writes
Ranges with no data render an honest empty state, not a zero that looks like a measurement
Tests cover a range with mixed priced and unpriced purchases
npm run test:run passes

userStories.title: Swift: mirror the pure modules against the shared fixtures
userStories.description: As an iOS developer, I want the Swift resolver, normalizer, unit converter and ledger fold to be provably identical to the TypeScript ones so that the platforms cannot drift.
acceptanceCriteria: Swift equivalents of itemNormalize, canonicalUnits, itemResolver and inventoryLedger live alongside the existing Ladder/ExposureLadderPolicy.swift pattern
A test target reads tests/fixtures/kitchen-loop/*.json directly and asserts the same expectations the TypeScript runner asserts
No fixture is duplicated or transformed for Swift; both platforms read the same files
The modules are pure and take their context as parameters, matching the TypeScript signatures

userStories.title: Release N+2: retire the legacy mirrors
userStories.description: As a platform engineer, I want the compatibility scaffolding removed once no shipped client depends on it, so the model stops carrying two truths.
acceptanceCriteria: BLOCKED until MIN_SUPPORTED_IOS_BUILD is past the release carrying US-683 through US-687; the story must not be started before that is true
Drops the direct-write translation trigger from US-668
Stops mirroring into foods.quantity, foods.is_safe and foods.is_try_bite; the columns themselves stay for one further release
The backward-compatibility suite from US-673 is retired in the same change with an explicit note saying why
